title: 24 Game
summary: Given an integer array cards of length 4, where each card contains a number in the range [1, 9], determine if you can arrange these numbers using the operators ['+', '-', '*', '/'] and parentheses '(' and ')' to achieve a value of 24.
statement: Given an integer array cards of length 4, where each card contains a number in the range [1, 9], determine if you can arrange these numbers using the operators ['+', '-', '*', '/'] and parentheses '(' and ')' to achieve a value of 24. The division operator '/' must perform real division, not integer division. Each operation must involve exactly two numbers. Unary minus is not allowed, and no two numbers can be concatenated to form a larger number. Return true if such an expression can be formed to equal 24, and false otherwise.
constraints: cards contains exactly four integers from 1 through 9.
Use every card once with +, -, *, /, and parentheses; intermediate fractions are allowed.
hints: Any expression combines two current values into one until a single value remains.
Backtrack over unordered pairs and all noncommutative operation orders.
Choose two, replace them with each possible result, and recurse.
Every binary expression tree has a final pairwise operation, so recursive pair reduction enumerates all valid expressions.
editorial: Every binary expression tree has a final pairwise operation, so recursive pair reduction enumerates all valid expressions.

tests.explanation: Eight minus four is four and seven minus one is six, whose product is twenty-four.
No ordering and operation combination reaches twenty-four.
